quote.text: Keeping more than one child's records straight in your head has stopped working.

promise.text: Homeschool record keeping for multiple children

lines.text: Two children, three subjects each, one shared afternoon.
File everything by child, log shared lessons once per child, and keep each record apart.

eyebrow.text: Set it up so it holds

head.text: Start one record per child from the first entry.

body.text: Splitting a shared page apart later means reading back through weeks of entries and guessing which line belonged to whom.

eyebrow.text: Set it up so it holds

head.text: Log a shared lesson once for each child in the room, in that child's own words for how it went.

body.text: A read-aloud, a science demonstration or a field trip counts once per child, not once for the group.

eyebrow.text: Set it up so it holds

head.text: Let each child's pace and curriculum stay fully separate.

body.text: One child a workbook behind the other, or on a different subject list entirely, needs no reconciling on the page.

eyebrow.text: Set it up so it holds

head.text: Keep a private note tied to the child it is about.

body.text: A note written about one child's reading is not evidence for a sibling, even if they read the same book.

eyebrow.text: Set it up so it holds

head.text: Print one child at a time.

body.text: A record with two children's names on one document is harder to read back and, for most evaluators, not what was asked for.

line.text: One page each morning that says what today looks like, per child.

title.text: Homeschool record keeping for multiple children

link.text: Free to read. Link in bio.
